title: No criminal liability in deaths of Diogo Jota and Andre Silva, Spanish court rules
content:
A Spanish court has ruled that there is no criminal liability over the car crash that killed Liverpool forward Diogo Jota and his brother Andre Silva in July.

Jota, 28, was driving himself and Silva, 25, when their car crashed in the province of Zamora, north-west Spain on July 3, 2025.

Investigators ruled that the Lamborghini suffered a high-speed blow out when overtaking another vehicle on the A-52 dual carriageway, causing it to crash into the central reservation and burst into flames.

After reviewing evidence from the scene and information from experts in road traffic collisions, the High Court of Justice for the region has determined that no criminal proceedings can be brought over the brothers’ deaths.

Sources from the Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Castilla y Leon told The Athletic: “The Court of First Instance in Puebla de Sanabria dismissed the case last November after assessing the documentary evidence in the file and, in particular, the expert reports issued by the Civil Guard’s Traffic Unit.

“The dismissal of the criminal proceedings does not preclude the possibility of the affected parties bringing a civil action to claim whatever they deem appropriate.”

Jota had been on his way back to England for the start of pre-season, having been advised not to fly following a minor procedure.

The Portugal international had just completed a successful season where he won the Nations League with Portugal and the Premier League with Liverpool.

Silva was also a professional footballer, who appeared for Porto as a youth-team player and was a first-team midfielder with FC Penafiel, a team in Portugal’s second tier, at the time of his death.

The funeral for the brothers was held on July 5 in their hometown Gondomar, Portugal, and was attended by many of Jota’s Liverpool and Portugal team-mates, including club head coach Arne Slot and national team head coach Roberto Martinez.

Tributes from across the football world flooded in for the pair after the news of their deaths, with Liverpool opening an in-person and online book of condolences outside Anfield.

Jota registered 65 goals and 26 assists in 182 games for Liverpool after signing from Wolverhampton Wanderers in September 2020. He made 37 appearances last season as Liverpool won their 20th league title.
